questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer instead of the traffic light. The officer's directions take priority over the signal.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let pedestrians, cyclists, and other vehicles in the intersection cross first. Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing before you proceed.

questions.question: If weather or light conditions require headlights while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You can only turn left when it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows that the road ahead will curve sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, reduce your speed to avoid hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, ease off the gas, do not brake hard, stay straight, and let the car slow down.

questions.question: Reaction time becomes slower after:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also makes it harder to see clearly and reduces your alertness. Alcohol impairs your judgment and driving skills. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, you should:

options.text: You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection. Always let pedestrians cross when turning on a green light.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car) can:

options.text: Never result in a traffic ticket.
Prevent someone from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upset other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating upsets other drivers and can lead to aggressive driving. Drivers can be ticketed for tailgating and unsafe driving.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians near the road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Slow down and pass with care.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with care.
questions.explanation: When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Watch for pedestrians who might cross into your path.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Lightly tap the brakes when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed significantly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign facing you, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must drive safely at all times.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicles.
questions.explanation: Follow motorcycles at least 3 to 4 seconds behind. Motorcycles can stop quickly, and following too close is dangerous. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid them. The risk of falls is highest on wet, icy, or gravel roads and on metal surfaces.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and showers do not speed up this process.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in the blood?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Honk your horn so they move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person crossing the street at a crosswalk or intersection, be careful and courteous. Let them cross safely before you proceed.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead of you to pick up or drop off children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back in.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must stop and wait. Do not go until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back. Even after the bus moves, wait to make sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about dangers ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: When it is raining or foggy, drivers should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see your vehicle, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to use while driving if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can reduce your ability to drive safely. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and nerves. It is illegal to drive while affected by any drug that impairs your driving, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has its red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and wait while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must let you go first.
You never need to let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass first. Once the intersection is clear and the signal allows, you may turn.

questions.question: To drive safely on the interstate, you must:

options.text: Be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving means you must stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds safely.

questions.question: Before changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, use your headlights:

options.text: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers cannot see your vehicle easily. Headlights make your vehicle more visible. If you turn on your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: You can tell if a driver is aggressive by:

options.text: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while driving. If you see a driver making sudden or improper lane changes, they may be aggressive. Do not engage with them. The best thing to do is move out of their way.
